name: @gymmap/server
//dev: `--env-file-if-exists` because the script could not start the server on its own: `loadAppConfig` never defaults a secret, so without the env file the boot fails on twelve required variables. It previously assumed the caller had already exported them, which is true of whoever set the shell up once and false of everybody else - including a restart after a crash. `-if-exists` rather than `--env-file` so a MISSING file still reaches the Zod error, which names the twelve variables and says to copy .env.example; a raw ENOENT would be a worse message than the one already written.
//: NOT type:module. NestJS + emitDecoratorMetadata is CommonJS territory; see packages/config/tsconfig/nest.json.

scripts.//test:contract: Was `echo "no-op"` while `test/auth-sessions.contract-spec.ts` sat beside it with nine passing assertions that NOTHING ran. The unit glob is `test/*.spec.ts` and that file ends `-spec.ts`, so it matched no suite and no CI job, and a green board said so. Wired to the layer the file's own header argues for rather than renaming it into the unit glob: it validates the generated OpenAPI document, which is a different question from what a handler does.
scripts.db:setup: prisma migrate deploy && docker exec -i gymmap-postgres psql -U postgres -d gymmap -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f - < ../../infra/compose/set-local-role-password.sql

//test:isolation: M-015 · ONE glob covering every *-spec.ts under test/isolation/. The previous form listed *.int-spec.ts and *.isolation-spec.ts explicitly, which silently excluded dropped-policy.negative-spec.ts — A7, the assertion that makes the other six falsifiable. A file that exists and is never run is the exact failure this milestone is about, and it was in the milestone's own script.
//lint: R1a keeps the ROOT devDependencies to seven packages, and eslint is not one of them — so each workspace that lints declares its own. The shared rule set still lives in one place (@gymmap/config/eslint); only the runner is per-package.
